title: Names, Bodies, and the Forming of Man
summary: How divine influx becomes named, garmented, molded, and lived through. T52 explains why divine beings are called gods, rich-men, and angels — three registers of one outgoing summoned by the next. T53 describes how the soul wears garments of light or darkness according to which principle its mysteries have agreed with. T54 narrates when the Lord's life is withdrawn from what the proprium had claimed, leaving the storehouses inactive. T55 expounds the building of the dwelling — how the Lord's operative power orders the rational into a house fit to receive him. T56 traces how the proprium mistakes the divine image and molds Adam as its counterfeit, with the Lord coming not to that molding but through it. T57 describes the senses set as rooms in the body, the heart as king and steward, with the Lord coming to take the keys. T58 explains why the lifespan of the first generations was so much greater than ours — the descent of governance through five orders.
organizing_principle: From naming (T52 three registers of emanation, T53 garments worn by the soul) through the central acts of light's coming and being claimed (T54-T55), to the actual forming of Adam (T56) and the senses (T57) and the diminishing lifespan (T58). The arc traces how divine influx becomes embodied, named, molded, and lived through in five-degree governance.
